channel.title: Corvus Arcade
channel.description: Most recent updates to Corvus Arcade.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
• Game closes or crashes: When a game is known to run better on the other graphics backend, its page now says so and switches with one click.
  • Controller compatibility: Use a Wine controller DLL beside this game's executable. Leave this off unless input is missing or mapped incorrectly.
  • 4 GB memory mode: Lets this 32-bit game use more address space. Corvus keeps an exact backup so the change can be reversed.
  • Metal trace capture: Records 20 seconds with Apple's Metal System Trace after the next launch. Use it only when investigating rendering stalls because capture adds overhead.
  • About Corvus Arcade: Run Windows games on your Apple Silicon Mac.

item.title: Version 0.9.0
item.description:
• Game support files: Installs the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime in this game's container. Use it only if the game reports a missing MSVCP or VCRUNTIME file.
  • Compatibility Assistant: Verified compatibility settings are available for this game.

item.title: Version 0.8.0
item.description:
• Quick Launch: Search games and actions
  • Save Data Vault: Corvus Arcade creates a safety restore point from the current saves first. The game must be closed.
  • Container Snapshots: Capture the full Windows container before experiments or major changes. APFS snapshots start quickly and use more space only as files change.
  • Compatibility Assistant: This game has been tested in Corvus Arcade. Updates can still change compatibility.
  • Tags: Add tags such as Co-op, Relaxing, Finished, or Family. Separate tags with commas.

item.title: Version 0.7.0
item.description:
• Install a game that comes in several parts: Point Corvus Arcade at a folder of numbered installer files and it checks them, says if one is missing or damaged, then runs the installer.
  • The installer window no longer opens behind the launcher: An installer's own window used to open behind the launcher, so it looked stuck while it waited for a click. It now comes to the front by itself.
  • Your game is found once the installer finishes: Corvus Arcade now waits for the installer to close before it looks, so it picks the game up on its own instead of asking you to find the program.
  • Installs no longer fail on the wrong drive: Installers used to offer a location macOS will not allow, then stop with an access error. They now start in a folder inside the game's own container.
  • A failed install says so: When an installer stops early, Corvus Arcade reports it instead of leaving an empty game in your library.
  • See what an install is doing: The launcher shows how much has been written, says when it is still unpacking, and tells you when nothing has happened for a few minutes.

item.title: Version 0.6.0
item.description:
• Take screenshots while you play: Press a shortcut during a game to capture its window, then browse the shots on the game's page in a viewer with a gallery and arrow keys.
  • Eight colour themes: Four dark and four light, chosen in Settings. The default is drawn from the app icon.
  • Favourites and search: Pin the games you play to the top of the library and the sidebar, search by name, and sort by last played, name or size.
  • Your saves are protected: Removing a game now asks first, says how many save files are at stake, and offers to export them before anything is deleted.
  • The Alt key reaches your games: Windows games can now receive Alt, which macOS previously kept for typing special characters. Games that bind Alt work without any setup.
  • Rename a game: Correct a name the store got wrong, or one taken from an archive filename.
  • Export your library: Save your game list, preferences and per-game settings to one small file, and restore them on another Mac.
  • DirectX 9 games are flagged: Corvus Arcade now reads what a game renders with and warns when neither graphics backend can run it, before you spend the download.

item.title: Version 0.5.0
item.description:
• Add a game straight from a zip or rar: Games that come as a compressed file with no installer now unpack on their own. Corvus Arcade finds the program inside and sets it up for you.
  • Check anti-cheat support before you install: Each game now shows whether its anti-cheat works on a Mac, so you know before you download instead of after.
  • Cover art and descriptions in your language: Cover art now comes straight from the store, so it stays current, and each game's description appears in the language you use Corvus Arcade in.
  • Use your own cover image: Right-click any game to choose your own cover or banner. You can restore the downloaded artwork at any time.
  • A hint when the other backend runs it better: When a game is known to run better on the other graphics backend, its page now says so and switches with one click.
  • Run games in a window: Games can now start windowed instead of taking over the whole screen.
  • Newer graphics engine: Corvus Arcade now ships Apple's latest Game Porting Toolkit, which improves compatibility and speed in many Direct3D games.

item.title: Version 0.4.3
item.description:
• Requires macOS 26 or later. Earlier versions could install the app but never actually run its graphics engine, so the requirement now matches reality.
  • The D3DMetal version picker shows which beta is bundled, and GPTK 4 is offered only on macOS 26.4 or later, where it can actually load.
  • Games that take their cover art from their own program now keep it, instead of rebuilding the artwork every time the library was opened.
  • A failed container setup now reports on the game it actually belongs to.

item.title: Version 0.4.2
item.description:
• Cover art for every game, taken from the program itself when the game is not on Steam.
  • A new Repair option restores missing fonts and re-applies per-game settings, fixing blank menus and unreadable text without removing anything you installed.
  • Drag a Windows program onto the library to add a game.
  • The library now shows the disk space each game uses, and the total across all of them.
  • MetalFX now takes effect on the DXMT backend, where it previously did nothing.
  • Launcher downloads now show sizes as well as a percentage, and a failed install offers a retry instead of looking finished.
  • Apple D3DMetal updated to Game Porting Toolkit 4.0 beta 2, verified working with a game. GPTK 3 remains the default, so nothing changes unless you switch.
  • Steam can be installed into its own container. The client works; individual games are unproven.

item.title: Version 0.4.1
item.description:
• A new app icon.
  • Change Game Executable now always shows what it found, with the program in use marked, instead of silently applying a single match and looking like nothing happened.

item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
• Your game is found for you. After an installer finishes, Corvus Arcade reads what it registered with Windows and sets the game's program automatically, so there is no more hunting for an .exe.
  • Pick a different program any time. A new Change Game Executable option lets you correct the launch target later, and Corvus Arcade warns you if the file you picked is a setup program.
  • Bottles are now called containers. The old name did not translate well in any language.
  • New games now use the recommended graphics backend by default, and a backend you pick when adding a game is actually applied.
  • Tested with a GOG installer (Brotato) in addition to Battle.net and Overwatch.
  • Many localization fixes: the site and app were showing English text in several languages.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
• Switch languages instantly. Corvus Arcade now speaks 33 languages, and you can change language in Settings without restarting the app.
  • Clear the shader cache. A new Settings button frees the disk space the Metal shader cache uses, and games rebuild it automatically on the next launch.
  • A redesigned Settings screen that matches the dark performance dashboard, with clearer graphics, game, and storage controls.
  • Dozens of localization fixes across all 33 languages.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
• A brand-new look. Corvus Arcade has been redesigned around a dark performance dashboard that keeps Play and your Mac's live status up front.
  • A new Home library. Every game and its status now show on a visual grid.
  • A live performance readout. A GPU and memory gauge sits right next to Play, with a rolling graph while you play.
  • Readiness checks with quick fixes. The game page flags things like tight memory and offers a one-tap fix before you play.
  • Everything organized into tabs. Overview, Graphics, Game settings, and Performance, so the setting you want is one click away.

item.title: Version 0.1.3
item.description:
• Game Settings, right in the launcher. Change a game's display mode, resolution, graphics quality, and frame-rate cap from Corvus Arcade, on the game's page.
  • Windowed mode. Games can open in a movable Mac window when the game itself is set to Windowed.
  • Various fixes and polish under the hood.

item.title: Version 0.1.2
item.description:
• Low-memory warning. On Macs with limited memory, Corvus Arcade now shows which apps are using the most, so you can close them for smoother play.
  • Free memory during play. Optionally close a game's launcher, like Battle.net, once the game starts, to free up memory. Turn it on in Settings.
  • Recommended in-game settings. Each game now lists the options that run best on Mac, right on its page.
  • Built-in performance log, so lag and stutter are easy to look into. Manage log space in Settings.
  • Smoother and more reliable under the hood.

item.title: Version 0.1.1
item.description:
• Snappier launching. The Play button responds the moment you click it, and shows a loading indicator while your game starts up.
  • Smarter window handling. Corvus Arcade steps aside only once your game is on screen, and comes right back when you close it.
  • Fewer permission pop-ups. Launching a game no longer keeps asking for access to your folders.
  • Smoother play. Your game keeps running smoothly even after your Mac clears out temporary files.
  • Update controls in Settings. Check for updates yourself, and turn automatic updates on or off.
  • Automatic updates are on by default, so you always have the latest alpha.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
• First public alpha
  • Tested with Battle.net and Overwatch on Apple Silicon
